messages:
maya: heads-up — our leak-detector flagged a public paste with a base64 blob that decodes to a GCP service-account key. appears tied to staging.
security-bot: [automated] leak-detector v2 found 1 potential credential exposure: https://paste.example/abcd (confidence: 0.82)
ian: thanks maya. can you drop the paste link here (without clicking) and the SA email if available?
maya: https://paste.example/abcd — decoded payload shows key for sa: staging-redis@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com
raj: i'm on rotation. quick triage Qs — is this key used by any prod infra or only staging jobs?
maya: only referenced in k8s configmap "staging-redis-creds" in the staging namespace. not in prod.
sylvia: good. still treat as sensitive. plan: (1) revoke & rotate key, (2) patch k8s, (3) audit read history, (4) tighten RBAC.
ops-oncall: i'll schedule a short maintenance window for config reloads in staging at 13:30 UTC if that works.
ian: steps i suggest —
- create new SA key (short-lived if possible)
- update configmap with new cred, rollout deployment with 0s maxUnavailable
- revoke leaked key in IAM
- enable Vault wrapping for the SA key material afterwards
- run audit queries in Cloud Audit Logs for IAM key usage
raj: agree. action owners: raj = rotate & revoke, sylvia = RBAC + Vault rewrap, ian = audit queries, maya = paste takedown & SRE notif.
maya: i've DM'd the paste host to takedown and filed a takedown ticket #TK-412.
ian: audit queries i'll run now — gcloud logging read 'protoPayload.methodName="google.iam.admin.v1.CreateServiceAccountKey" AND resource.labels.service_account_id="staging-redis"' --limit 50 --format json
ian: also will look for token usage: gcloud logging read 'protoPayload.methodName="google.iam.admin.v1.SignJwt" OR protoPayload.methodName: "oauth"' --start-time "2026-03-20T00:00:00Z" --end-time "2026-03-21T12:00:00Z"
raj: creating replacement key now. using short TTL key via workload-identity where possible. if the app can use workload identity, prefer that instead of long-lived keys.
sylvia: policy change: restrict iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken to CI service accounts only, remove broad iam.serviceAccounts.actAs bindings in staging. i'll prepare a policy diff.
ops-oncall: 13:30 UTC window confirmed. i'll post in #staging-alerts and do a quick configmap rollout script: kubectl -n staging rollout restart deploy/staging-redis
raj: created new key, uploaded to Vault transit-wrapped blob under secret path secret/data/staging/redis-sa. command used to wrap: 
```
vault write transit/encrypt/sa-keys plaintext=$(base64 < new-key.json)
```
updated k8s to reference Vault via CSI driver.
maya: pasted takedown confirmed (host removed). good.
ian: audit results — the compromised key shows no token exchanges outside our CI runner IP range. last use was 2026-03-19 08:21 UTC by ci-runner-5. no sign of external exfiltration.
sylvia: still proceed with full revoke. RBAC patch ready: will remove roles/storage.objectViewer from staging-redis-sa and add a scoped role storage.staging-redis-readonly with condition on principal.email == "ci-runner@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
raj: revoked leaked key at iam admin console. command: gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete "<LEAKED_KEY_ID>" --iam-account=staging-redis@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com
ops-oncall: applied configmap update, restarted deployment, pods are coming up healthy. no errors in the first 5m.
ian: cross-checking Cloud Audit logs for any anomalous egress — nothing unusual. also checked VPC flow logs for external destinations, all internal.
maya: quick note for postmortem — how did credential get to paste? looks like dev accidentally cat'd key while troubleshooting and pasted. will remind team about ephemeral creds and gitignore.
sylvia: i opened a short-lived org policy to enforce centrally-managed secrets: disallow creation of keys unless request has JIRA ticket and approver label. implementing conditional IAM binding for key creation via org policies.
raj: follow-up: recommend migrating staging workloads to Workload Identity — timeline proposal 2 weeks. opens up ability to retire static keys entirely.
ian: i'll attach audit queries + saved filters to the incident ticket.
ops-oncall: filing incident ticket SEC-2026-87 for the rotation/cleanup. tagging all owners.
maya: thanks all. after action items: run a tabletop on accidental paste scenarios, update onboarding checklist to include 'never paste credentials', and add an automated scanner to block pastes that match sa key regex in internal chat. :thumbsup:
sylvia: assigning postmortem lead to maya. please include timeline, root cause, and remediation verification steps.
security-bot: [automated] Incident SEC-2026-87 created and assigned to maya. Reminder: attach audit exports and rotation evidence within 48h.
raj: closing loop — revoked key, new key in Vault, k8s now uses Vault CSI, RBAC tightened, audits attached. marking my tasks done.
ops-oncall: last check 13:50 UTC — staging looks stable. closing maintenance window.
maya: will draft postmortem and TL;DR for leadership. thanks folks.
